t: A county on the Scheldt and Sambre, ruled from Mons and Valenciennes, within the Holy Roman Empire but facing France.
Its counts became Latin emperors of Constantinople and married into the French and English royal houses.
Absorbed by Burgundy in 1433 and partly lost to France in 1659–1678, it was annexed by revolutionary France in 1795.
dyk: Philippa of Hainaut, queen of Edward III, took the Valenciennes chronicler Jean Froissart into her service, giving him access to the English court for his chronicles.
ev: Reginar Longneck holds comital power in Hainaut
Countess Richilde marries Baldwin of Flanders
Count Baldwin VI becomes the first Latin emperor of Constantinople
John II of Avesnes unites Hainaut with Holland and Zeeland
Philippa of Hainaut marries Edward III of England
Jacqueline of Bavaria surrenders Hainaut to Philip the Good of Burgundy
The Treaty of Nijmegen confirms the French conquest of southern Hainaut
Revolutionary France annexes Hainaut as the department of Jemmapes
